newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SOCCER-CONTRACTORS LOOKING FOR RARE FULL HOUSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CONTRACTORS LOOKING FOR RARE FULL HOUSE.

text.p: Egyptian soccer club Arab Contractors are hoping for a rare capacity crowd to propel them to victory in the African Cup Winners' Cup on Friday.
The Cairo team meet Sodigraf of Zaire at the National stadium in Cairo in the second leg of the final, having forced a goalless draw away in Kinshasa in the first leg last month.

Arab Contractors, despite two previous African cup titles, live in the shadow of the more illustrious city neighbours, Al Ahly and Zamalek, and hardly enjoy the vociferous support and passion that surrounds one of the world's most intense footballing rivalries.
But Contractors are hoping to entice a full house to the imposing Cairo venue on Friday afternoon by slashing ticket prices to as low as a single Egyptian pound (about 35 US cents).
"They are hoping for a big crowd because they never really get much support," said a spokesman for the Confederation of African Football in Cairo.

Contractors, who won the Cup Winners' Cup in 1982 and 1983, are comfortably placed for a third triumph in the competition -- and possibly the first half of an Egyptian double in the two major African club competitions this year.
Zamalek host Shooting Stars on December 13 in the second leg of the African Champions Cup final, having been beaten 2-1 by the Nigerian team in the first leg in Ibadan last Saturday.
Contractors are expected to play a much more open match than their defensive approach in the first leg, with Egyptian international Ahmed Nakhla and Abdel Sattar Sabry key to their plans.
Sabry's tricky running was one of Egypt's highlights in the African Nations Cup finals in South Africa at the start of the year.
Their Zairian opposition have made a dramatic transformation over the last seven years from a factory team into African club competition finalists under ambitious club president Patcheli Makengo.
Their striker Mbilua Tondelua is the leading goalscorer in all three of the African club competitions this year with nine goals in seven matches.
